entries.text: This message is being sent from the Community Code of Conduct Committee, with the approval of the Core Team. As part of the Community CoC policy, the Committee membership is to be refreshed on an annual basis. We are seeking up to 3 volunteers to serve on the Committee for the coming year, January 1, 2027 - December 31, 2027. We are seeking people who reflect the diversity of the PostgreSQL community, with the goal to have members from multiple countries and varied demographics. The time commitment for Committee involvement varies, based on internal administrative work and the number of active investigations. We estimate an average of 5 to 10 hours per month, but that could increase if there is an increase in the number of incident reports. If you are interested, please complete the questionnaire below, and email your responses to the Committee at coc@postgresql.org no later than December 7, at 05:00 PM UTC. The Questionnaire Your name: Current employer: Current country of residence: (We ask for employer and residence because one of the goals of the Committee is to have representation from a variety of geographical areas. We also want to avoid a concentration of members from one company.) What interests you about being on the CoC Committee? Have you been on another CoC Committee/team, or had a similar role at another organization? (Prior experience is not required, it's just helpful to know everyone's background.) entries.summary: We are very glad to announce the Distributed E-Maj 0.9.1 version.
entries.text: We are very glad to announce the Distributed E-Maj 0.9.1 version. Distributed E-Maj is an add-on to the E-Maj solution that brings the capability to revert data changes recorded on several databases to a common stable state in a consistent manner. This is the first released version. Thus, it is delivered for test purpose only. Distributed E-Maj 0.9.1 is compatible with E-Maj 5.0.1 and supports 14 to 19 PostgreSQL versions. The full documentation is available on line. The core extension is available at pgxn.org for installation or github.org for development. As a reminder, E-Maj is a "Change Data Capture" solution offering multiple ways to use tracked changes: consultation, statistics, replay, and above all rollback (E-Maj rollback) to a stable state (Mark) of predefined sets of database tables (Table Groups), allowing your data to "travel through time" in an optimized and consistent way. Distributed E-Maj extends the concept of a "Mark" and the "E-Maj Rollback" to table groups spread across multiple databases. Any feedback is welcome !
entries.title: Announcing the first Distributed E-Maj version.

entries.summary: PGConf.dev 2027 (May 11-14, 2027, Montréal, CA), aka PostgreSQL Developer Conference 2027, is the annual gathering of PostgreSQL community organizers, hackers, extension maintainers, and the developers who build on…
entries.text: PGConf.dev 2027 (May 11-14, 2027, Montréal, CA), aka PostgreSQL Developer Conference 2027, is the annual gathering of PostgreSQL community organizers, hackers, extension maintainers, and the developers who build on their work. Join us for four days of unconference sessions, workshops, hallway-track conversations, and talks that focus on building the future of PostgreSQL. The call for proposals is open through January 12, 2027! We're looking for presentations (25 and 50 minutes), workshops, panels, posters, and other content focused on PostgreSQL development: patches and extensions, performance and architectural work, missing features and unmet user needs, lessons from production, research, community organizing, and more! A full list of ideas is available on the CFP page. Community Discussion Sessions are interactive sessions where you can discuss ideas for PostgreSQL development and community in a meeting format. This year, discussion proposals are accepted in two rounds: the first round closes with the main CFP on January 12, 2027, and the second round closes on April 13, 2027. If you would like to present a poster, please let us know by March 15, 2027. Have a topic you want to see at PGConf.dev? You can suggest it, or upvote other suggestions, through the Talk Solicitation Program. Even if you've never presented at a PostgreSQL event before, we'd love to hear your ideas and can provide feedback on your proposal! You can submit your content proposals here: https://2027.pgcon
entries.title: PGConf.dev 2027 Call for Proposals is Open

entries.summary: We are pleased to announce that the Call for Papers for Nordic PGDay 2027 is now open.
entries.text: We are pleased to announce that the Call for Papers for Nordic PGDay 2027 is now open. The conference will take place in Stockholm, Sweden on March 16, continuing the tradition of bringing together PostgreSQL users, developers, and enthusiasts from across the Nordic region and beyond. The Call for Papers will remain open until 8 January 2027, and all speakers will be informed about the selection results by 28 January 2027. For 2027 the program has been expanded to a one-and-a-half track community format, complemented by an additional half-track dedicated to our sponsors. This structure allows us to accommodate a greater number of high-quality talks. Speaking at Nordic PGDay is an excellent opportunity to present your work to a knowledgeable and engaged audience, contribute to the growth of the community, and connect with peers from across the region. We would also like to invite companies and organizations to consider sponsoring Nordic PGDay 2027. Sponsorship offers an opportunity to connect with the PostgreSQL community, increase visibility among users and developers, and support the continued success of community-driven PostgreSQL events. For more information please visit our sponsors page. Information about the CfP committee, including the members responsible for reviewing proposals, is available on the conference website.
entries.title: Nordic PGDay 2027 - Call for Papers & Sponsors!

entries.summary: November 19, 2026 - The PostgreSQL Global Development Group today announced the release of PostgreSQL 19, the latest version of the world's most advanced open source database.
entries.text: November 19, 2026 - The PostgreSQL Global Development Group today announced the release of PostgreSQL 19, the latest version of the world's most advanced open source database. Mission-critical usage of PostgreSQL continues to rapidly rise, and PostgreSQL 19 responds to this by simplifying both administration and development for these workloads at scale. This release introduces the REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) command so users can optimize tables for their current workload without disruption to ongoing operations. PostgreSQL 19 gives users better control over plan stability and query performance with the new pg_plan_advice extension. Developers will find many delightful features in this release, from support for "read-your-writes" consistency on standbys to "get or create" behavior that saves a network round trip. "For over 30 years, the global open source community has built PostgreSQL into a database that organizations trust with their most critical data," said Jonathan Katz, a member of the PostgreSQL core team. "PostgreSQL 19 continues that commitment to reliability, giving users new ways to manage their workloads without disruption and to build applications that span multiple systems." PostgreSQL, an innovative data management system known for its reliability, robustness, and extensibility, benefits from 30 years of open source development from a global developer community and has become the preferred open source relational database for organizations of all sizes. entries.summary: The WAL-G team is pleased to announce the release of WAL-G 3.0.10. WAL-G is an open-source backup and recovery tool for PostgreSQL, Apache Cloudberry, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB, Redis, and other databases.
entries.text: The WAL-G team is pleased to announce the release of WAL-G 3.0.10. WAL-G is an open-source backup and recovery tool for PostgreSQL, Apache Cloudberry, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB, Redis, and other databases. The main new PostgreSQL feature is wal-send. It serves archived WAL over PostgreSQL's streaming replication protocol, allowing standbys and pg_receivewal to read WAL directly from object storage and follow new segments as they arrive. Other PostgreSQL improvements include: Continuous WAL archival in daemon mode: the pipeline keeps working between requests, and retained lookahead reduces directory scanning (#2697, #2698). Optional backup-push --wait-for-archive: WAL-G waits for all WAL segments required by the backup to reach the selected backup storage before publishing the backup as complete (#2722). Backup-name reservation before upload, protecting against concurrent reuse of the same name (#2707). WAL prefetch files are published only after a successful download (#2696), and WAL source files are closed after upload failures (#2695). Standard X/X LSN notation in catchup-push --from-lsn (#2643). S3 support now uses AWS SDK v2 and adds configurable request timeouts, retryable error codes, and checksum settings. Backup copying can use server-side S3 copy and configurable transfer concurrency. entries.summary: pgjumbo is a new desktop client for PostgreSQL 12+, free to use, for Windows, macOS and Linux, with query, data and administration tools.
entries.text: pgjumbo is a new desktop client for PostgreSQL 12+, free to use, for Windows, macOS and Linux, with query, data and administration tools. pgjumbo connects to PostgreSQL 12+, including Amazon Aurora and RDS with IAM authentication, directly, over SSL or through an SSH tunnel. Installers are available for Windows (x64 and ARM64), macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) and Linux (AppImage, .deb and .rpm). Version 1.0.2 includes: An object explorer and inspector with each object's CREATE script, statistics and dependencies. A Query Tool with completion, syntax errors from PostgreSQL's own parser as you type, parameters, EXPLAIN as a table or a diagram, and results that can be sorted, filtered, compared and exported. A data editor that shows the statements before it saves them. Backup and restore built on pg_dump, pg_dumpall and pg_restore: choosing objects and rows, server backups as a folder of archives, reading an archive's contents before restoring, and restoring into a new database. Maintenance: what each table needs and what holds VACUUM back, VACUUM, ANALYZE and REINDEX as reviewed steps with progress, and autovacuum settings per table. Server activity, configuration, roles and privileges, logs, replication, pg_cron jobs and LISTEN/NOTIFY. Changes to objects are shown as SQL and reviewed before they run, and on servers marked Production, destructive statements ask for confirmation first. Download pgjumbo · Release notes for 1.0.2
entries.title: pgjumbo: a new free desktop client for PostgreSQL

entries.summary: CortexRidge has released pgSherpa, a free desktop companion for PostgreSQL on macOS, now available on the Mac App Store.
entries.text: CortexRidge has released pgSherpa, a free desktop companion for PostgreSQL on macOS, now available on the Mac App Store. pgSherpa sits in a corner of the screen and polls one or more PostgreSQL servers (PostgreSQL 12 to 18). When something needs attention it says so in a sentence, with the rows behind it: Health: lock-wait chains, long-running and idle-in-transaction sessions, replication lag and replication slots, vacuum and transaction ID wraparound, connection limits. Security: the server's version compared with the latest PostgreSQL minor release and the CVEs fixed since, plus configuration such as SSL, MD5 passwords and superuser count. Cloud: backups, failovers, maintenance windows and replicas for DigitalOcean Managed Databases, Supabase and Amazon RDS / Aurora PostgreSQL, read from the provider's API. SQL: a query box with PostgreSQL completion and \h syntax help for the server's own version. Every statement runs in a read-only transaction unless the user switches it to write. Reports: ready-made views of pg_stat_activity, pg_locks, pg_stat_statements, vacuum progress, indexes and replication. pgSherpa needs only a role with pg_monitor. It installs no extension and no agent on the server, and it has no account and no telemetry; passwords and keys stay in the macOS Keychain. It runs on macOS 12 or later, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Mac App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6833955115 More information: https://cortexridge.com/
entries.title: pgSherpa: a free PostgreSQL monitoring companion for macOS

entries.summary: We are pleased to announce the release 1.1.1 of PG_CVE, a lightweight tool designed to provide DBAs and system administrators with a clear, up-to-date overview of CVEs (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures), known…
entries.text: We are pleased to announce the release 1.1.1 of PG_CVE, a lightweight tool designed to provide DBAs and system administrators with a clear, up-to-date overview of CVEs (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures), known exploits, and release stability across PostgreSQL versions. Key Features & Highlights: Rapid tracking of security advisories and CVEs associated with specific PostgreSQL versions. Overview of release stability and patch information to assist DBAs with upgrade planning. Security context: integration of known exploit data for accurate vulnerability triage. Lightweight, standalone web interface for fast client-side navigation. Links & Resources: Live Interactive Demo: https://meob.github.io/PG_CVE/?version=15.8 Source Code & Documentation: https://github.com/meob/PG_CVE
entries.title: PG_CVE 1.1.1 Released

entries.summary: pg_fastload 1.0.0 is a parallel bulk loader for PostgreSQL, 1.58x faster than the best pg_bulkload mode and 6.07x faster than COPY.
entries.text: pg_fastload 1.0.0 is a parallel bulk loader for PostgreSQL, 1.58x faster than the best pg_bulkload mode and 6.07x faster than COPY. It parallelises the loading pipeline across background workers while keeping the load inside a single transaction. It is a source-level fork of pg_bulkload 3.1.23, so control-file syntax, TYPE values, log format and WRITER modes are unchanged. Repository: github.com/yuansong/pg_fastload Release: pg_fastload v1.0.0 License: BSD 3-Clause, with the upstream pg_bulkload copyright notices retained The problem pg_bulkload and COPY both run the whole load in one backend: read, parse, form the tuple, write. On a 16-core machine that leaves 15 cores idle, and the parse step is usually the expensive one. For CSV it is a byte-at-a-time state machine followed by a type input function per column. How it works The load has four stages: read input, parse record and split fields, form the tuple, and insert. Stages 1-3 move to background workers; stage 4 stays serial in the backend that issued the load: one reader worker -> N parser workers -> leader writes Design points that matter in practice: The input file is read exactly once. A single reader scans sequentially and hands chunks to the workers over shm_mq; the workers never open the file. Total read volume stays at 1x the file size, so the speedup does not invert once the data is larger than the page cache. It is still one transaction.
